## Caller contract
`withAuth`-wrapped routes in `pages/api/accounting/bank/*` (+ `bank-match-confirm.ts`); migrations `327_*` (VAT subtype), `514/515/519/520/526`, `*bank_*`. Every DB function takes `companyId` first. VLM services are stateless; the caller persists under its own `companyId`.

## Main function signatures
- `lockBankTransactionForUpdate(companyId, txId)` — company-scoped `FOR UPDATE`; `null` for missing/other tenant; THROWS outside a request transaction (an implicit one locks nothing); 5s `lock_timeout` → `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError` (test with `isBankTransactionLockTimeout`, structural), restored to `DEFAULT` on the SUCCESS path — `SET LOCAL` lasts to the end of the TRANSACTION, and both confirm arms and `voidPaymentDocument` call this FIRST, so without the restore the 5s budget governs every lock they take afterwards (pinned both ways — present on success, ABSENT after a 55P03, because in a `finally` it would raise 25P02 over the typed error — in `tests/unit/services/bankAllocationRowLock.test.ts`).
- `allocateTransaction(companyId, txId, …, opts?)` / `splitAllocateTransaction` — post the JE; VAT account via `systemAccountResolver` (subtype) then codes 1140/2120. Its two pre-write refusals (missing row, status ≠ `imported`) throw `BankAllocationRefusal` — `isBankAllocationRefusal`.
- `reverseReconciledTransaction(companyId, txId, userId, opts?: {postingAgent?, reversalDate?})` — unwind, contra, reset to `imported`, ALL in one savepoint. Contra date = original entry's when that period is open, else today. Refuses PRE-WRITE on a closed/locked period; `no_period` is not refused (`createJournalEntry` auto-creates the year). Omit `postingAgent` and the contra stays `human:<userId>`.
- `validateBankSupplierPayment` / `planSupplierAllocationLines` / `planSupplierPaymentApplication` (in `ap/`) throw `SupplierPaymentRefusal` for a refusal and NOTHING ELSE — catch that, re-throw the rest, or a dropped connection reaches the browser as a 400. `planSupplierPaymentApplication` was the exception until 2026-09-10: it threw bare `Error`s, and `supplier-allocations.ts` therefore had to catch EVERYTHING and answer 400 with `err.message` — schema and column names in front of the user, on a status `withAuth` COMMITs, monitored as their mistake. Typing the four throws is what let that catch be narrowed, so the two changes only make sense together.
- `findBankTransactionsByReferences(companyId, refs[], acct?)` — ONE query (join on `unnest($refs)`, two arms, one per column), `Map` by trimmed reference, 25 candidates per reference, each carrying `matchedReference`+`matchedColumn`. Returns every candidate; the caller decides what >1 means. `findBankTransactionAllocationStates(companyId, ids[])` — `{id,status,matchedJournalLineId}` for a whole set in one query; it reads BOTH columns deliberately — a row carrying `matched_journal_line_id` is in the ledger whatever `status` says, and **a fixture that sets only the status passes while production fails**. `bulk_allocate_bank_transactions` calls it once for up to `MAX_BANK_LINES_PER_REQUEST` (6, `src/lib/limits/authorityHoldLimits.ts`) resolved ids before it posts anything — one request holds the company authority key for every line it posts, which is what that cap bounds. `getBankTransactionStatus` stays for one-line tools, and exists so an MCP refusal can be answered from a READ: both write services write BEFORE they can fail, and a refusal frees the idempotency key, so the retry writes a second time.
- **Bulk/batch path**: `contactDirectoryService.suppliersBelongToCompany(companyId, ids[])` / `customersBelongToCompany` — ONE query per set, empty set skipped; the bulk allocate loop depends on them, and checking a counterparty per line is 500 round trips. `partitionAllocationLines` (`allocationApplyRoute`) is what REFUSES on that path, pre-write, splitting the lines into postable and skipped — `invoiceSkipReason` beside it is exported and called by nothing.
- `importBankStatement` / `importParsedTransactions(…, {skipAutoPost, skipPostImportEffects})`, `importStatementForAgent`, `undoImportBatch` (null for another company; deletes only `imported` rows, reports the rest), `startReconciliation`/`completeReconciliation`/`createAdjustmentEntry`, `applyRules` (priority ASC = highest), `listAgentPostings` (`reversed` from `reversed_at`, never `status`), `buildExpenseJournalFromReceipt` (pure), `extractWithVlm`/`extractBankStatementWithVlm`/`extractStatutoryDocWithVlm`.
- `tableLockUnavailable()` (`bankTxLock`) — `LOCK TABLE bank_transactions IN ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE NOWAIT` under its OWN savepoint. `true` = a DDL-mode lock is held on the TABLE. `matchTransaction` asks it before reading a `55P03` as "line claimed", because the match UPDATE runs under `withBankLockBudget`'s 5s `lock_timeout`, which bounds every wait THAT statement takes and so fires on an index build too (the row lock restores the default after itself, so nothing else in the request inherits the budget); refused → `BankMatchUnavailableError` ("retry in a moment"), counted as `skippedUnavailable`, never `skippedRaced`. It cannot be consulted from `lockBankTransactionForUpdate` itself — that SELECT is outside a savepoint, so its 55P03 aborts the tx and the probe answers 25P02 (K-140).
- `rulePattern(rule)` (`bankRulesSuggestionPass`) — the ONE place a rule row becomes an ILIKE pattern, for BOTH arms. `match_type` is nullable and NULL means `exact`; `String(rule.match_type)` reads `'null'` and widens it to `contains`.
- `getAutoPostSettings`/`updateAutoPostSettings`/`autoPostRunSnapshot`/`sweep` (`autoPostGateService`), `undoRun(companyId, runId, userId)` (`autoPostUndoService` — one savepoint per row; a contended/failed/reconciled row is skipped and counted per reason (`skippedBy`), and the run is marked undone ONLY when `skipped` is 0 (`undone` in the result). A provisional JE already reversed by hand is finished without a second reversal (`alreadyUndone`); a row still `allocated`/`matched` with nothing linked is a `failed` skip, never already-undone. Throws the contention — `bank-auto-post` 409 — only when no row was written at all; otherwise 200 with the counts. Each row is locked and re-read first; a row a later journal may already correct is an `offsetByHand` skip, described in `handOffsets` (line and journal: date, amount, description), and nothing is posted for it). Two recorded decisions (`bank-auto-post` `confirmHandCorrection` / `undoAnyway`, both `audit_log`, both close the run when no row is left tagged): `markCorrectedByHand` posts nothing and is accepted only for a person-made journal that, with the posting, nets every non-bank account of it to zero (within a cent); `undoAnyway` declares the journal unrelated and undoes the line. Refusals are `HandCorrectionRefusedError` (400, pre-write).

## Business rules
- **A bank account is a `gl_accounts` row with `account_subtype='bank'`** — `bank_transactions.bank_account_id` FKs to `gl_accounts(id)`; the name misleads. The `bank_accounts` table is vestigial (0 rows prod); only `bank_feed_connections` may point at it. Use `hasBankAccount`/`countBankAccounts`, never a count of `bank_accounts`.
- Status flow `imported → matched → allocated → reconciled`; allocation is atomic under `withTransaction` (JE + status).
- **Direction follows the SIGN of the line, on every arm.** `isSpent = amount < 0` decides DR/CR for supplier and customer allocations too — a refund booked as a payment moves the bank by TWICE the line (R261,651.64 found on Velocity). The VAT KEY follows the alloc TYPE, not the direction (a refund reverses INPUT tax). The 4-way match runs only when `isSpent`; a `customer_payments` row is minted only when `!isSpent`. Every settler asks `signMismatchReason` (`bankLineDirection`) — it refuses a ZERO line outright, because the downstream throw it fronts would land mid-write.
- **A VAT code on a supplier/customer allocation posts NO VAT** (control-account settlement): one predicate, `gl/settlementVat.isControlAccountSettlement`, read by `allocateTransaction` and by `gl/ruleVatResolution` for the sweep. `allocateTransaction` ANDs it with `Boolean(entityId)` (an entity-less call falls through to the account arm); the rule path picks on `allocType` alone. `gl/bankContraVat` drops the code on a `bank`-subtype contra — pass that flag as `undefined` when the account is absent from the map, never `?? false`.
- **Attended paths never coerce a VAT choice; `autoPostRuleLine` (unattended) does** and returns `vatDenied` (from the account's `vat_input_denied` flag, tallied into `autoPostVatDenied`); the unattended line builder is `buildAutoCreateLines` (`bankRulesMatchingHelpers`), which is where the `netAmount` defect lived. `auto_create_entry=false` rules are suggestion-only. BOTH directions are pinned by `tests/unit/services/bankVatDisplayAgreesWithJournalDb.test.ts` (real Postgres) — it is the only gate on this rule, so don't delete it when a mock would be quicker.
- **A settlement must write its payment DOCUMENT and its ALLOCATION row** — `supplier_payments` + `payment_allocations` on the AP side, `customer_payments` + `customer_payment_allocations` on the AR side. Those are the only tables `bankAllocationUnwind` reads, so a bare `amount_paid` write is irreversible — and, computed in JS, a lost update too. Both arms of `bank-match-confirm` obey this: `confirmSupplierMatch` → `applyBankLineToSupplierInvoices`, `confirmCustomerMatch` → `confirmReceiptMatch`. Never assign `supplier_invoices.balance` (GENERATED since mig 201 → 428C9). **An over-payment is REFUSED, not capped, on both arms**: `apAgingService` and `debtorsManagerService` read the invoice tables alone, so the excess would part the control account from the aging invisibly. A caller that HANDS IN allocations (the MCP apply tool) may leave a remainder; a screen deriving them may not.
- **`withAuth` COMMITs below 500**, so every refusal must be decided from READS before the first write; past the first write the only safe answer is 500. Exception, and it must be shown: a refusal raised before any write may keep a 4xx (`bank-match-confirm` answers 409 on a contended line).
- **Every pg error aborts the transaction**, not just 40P01/40001/25P02 — so a swallowed failure needs a SAVEPOINT, not a code whitelist (`bankTransferAutoLink`, the import auto-post sweep). If the savepoint's own ROLLBACK fails, rethrow: nothing saves that case. Give each savepoint a unique name; a duplicate SHADOWS rather than errors.
- **Row locks**: LOCKED — `allocateTransaction`, `splitAllocateTransaction`, `reverseReconciledTransaction`, `matchTransaction`, `unmatchTransaction`, `excludeTransaction`, each auto-post candidate. NOT locked, deliberately — read-only paths, the post-UPDATE re-read, `deleteTransactions` (its `status='imported'` predicate is the guard) and `bulkAcceptTransactions` (it knowingly relabels allocated rows). `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` is re-issued EVERY call, never memoised: it is subtransaction-aware and `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` restores `0`. Bulk loops sort by transaction id — a total lock order turns a deadlock into a wait. A raced/locked row is SKIPPED and counted (`skippedRaced`, `autoPostSkippedLocked`, `autoPostTruncatedRules`; `MAX_RULE_CANDIDATES`=500), never allowed to abort the run, and every counter reaches the UI.
- **CANONICAL LOCK ORDER — every path takes these rows in this sequence, always**: (1) `bank_transactions`, (2) `customer_payments`/`supplier_payments`, (3) `customer_invoices`/`supplier_invoices` (a SET of them `ORDER BY id`), (4) `gl_journal_entries`/`gl_journal_lines`. Two paths taking any pair in opposite orders deadlock: Postgres kills a victim with **40P01**, which `withAuth` answers as a 500 — the money path reporting a server fault to a user whose only mistake was arriving at the same instant as somebody else.

  **Build this table MECHANICALLY, never by reasoning about which pairs can run together.** An `UPDATE` and a `DELETE` take a row lock exactly as `FOR UPDATE` does, so enumerating only the explicit `FOR UPDATE`s is what hid three inversions across rounds 7–9 — `voidSupplierPayment` was missing from this very table while it deadlocked. The enumeration walks every function that touches more than one of these relations (`FOR UPDATE`, `LOCK TABLE`, the `lock*ForUpdate` helpers, `fetch{Invoice,Bill}Candidates`, and every `UPDATE`/`DELETE`), records the ORDERED sequence, and derives the cycles from that LIST. A path you did not list cannot be checked.

  **The one exemption, and it is structural rather than an unreachability argument**: a row INSERTed by this transaction cannot be locked by any other transaction, because no other transaction can see it. So `createJournalEntry` + `postJournalEntry` on a brand-new entry does not put `gl_journal_entries` into a path's ordering; a `FOR UPDATE` or reversal of a PRE-EXISTING entry does. That is the difference between `confirmCustomerPayment` (exempt) and `cancelCustomerPayment` (not).

Undoing a posted allocation is `reverseReconciledTransaction`'s job.
- **Dedup is a CONTENT HASH of (date, amount, description, balance)** — no reference in it, so two genuinely separate same-day identical rows collapse (known). Do NOT add the reference: pre-2026-09-07 rows carry none and would stop matching their own statement. Known: the 2026-08-27 `parseAmount` comma fix MOVED the hash, so re-importing an SA-formatted CSV lands the corrected row beside the wrong one — undo the batch first.

So `reference` wins outright and `bank_reference` is consulted only for a reference that matched nothing. Mig 519's expression indexes must stay character-for-character identical to the query or the planner reverts to a company scan — `bankTxRefCandidateQuery` is exported UNRUN so the DB-gated test can `EXPLAIN` the service's REAL statement; the previous test planned a pasted copy and stayed green through a regression. Cancelling releases `matched` rows to `imported` and merely detaches `allocated`/`provisional`/`excluded`; it re-asserts `status='in_progress'` in the DELETE. Cancel's `dry_run` runs every guard and writes nothing, and a POSTED adjustment journal blocks the cancel — found through `gl_journal_entries.source_record_id`. Adjustments use mig 526's own column, NOT `source_document_id` (FK'd to `captured_documents` since mig 409).
- Coverage/cash: `cash.balance.v1` (ledger) is `cashBalanceService`, `cash.statement.v1` (sum of `bank_transactions.amount`) is a different question — never net them. The OTHER services answering the statement question are `bankAccountStatusService.balance` and `kpiDashboardService`; add a fifth cash answer in neither. `kpiChartsService` is the mirror of the LEFT-JOIN-ON-vs-WHERE rule below and drifts with it. `bt.amount = jl.debit - jl.credit` on all 9,097 matched prod rows, so `glOnlyMovement - statementOnlyMovement` is an EXACT identity; a non-zero `unexplainedResidual` means a `bank_opening_balance` with no journal behind it. Neither service filters `is_active` (a deactivated account still holds cash — `deactivatedWithBalance` REPORTS them, it does not exclude them); `getCashBalance` spans subtype `bank` AND `cash`; the posted/date restriction belongs in the LEFT JOIN's ON + a CASE, never a WHERE (that deletes draft-only accounts).
- `getCashBalance(companyId, asOf, { exclusive: true })` answers the OPENING balance — the closing balance of the day BEFORE `asOf`. An option, not a day the caller subtracts: JS date arithmetic on this UTC+2 server is what put 291 journals in the wrong period. `cashFlowDirectService.fetchOpeningCash` delegates here rather than keeping its own copy.
- Display columns come from the POSTED JOURNAL, never a cached label: `ALLOCATED_ACCOUNT_LATERAL` (with `AND bl.gl_account_id = bt.bank_account_id` — load-bearing, or the sibling of a user-picked line reads as the destination) and `POSTED_VAT_LATERAL` (`'standard'` asserted from the presence of a VAT-account line, NULL over zero lines). Mig 520's `allocation_rule_{id,name}` carry the rule; `allocated_entity_name` is ALWAYS the account. `allocation_batch_id` is CLEARED by allocate/split/reverse, or a batch reverse would unwind a posting it never made (mig 514/515). `recordAllocationBatchLines` THROWS unless every id was stamped — a posted journal outside the reversible set is the failure the batch id exists to prevent; `getAllocationBatchLines` LEFT-joins (returning `transactionExists`) and returns `null` for another tenant's batch so the caller renders the generic NOT_FOUND.
- Dates: build journal dates with `fmtDate` from `@/lib/neon`, never `toISOString()` — pg returns `transaction_date` at LOCAL midnight and UTC rendering dates a 00:30 SAST line to the previous day (wrong month at a period boundary). `getBankTransactions` pages on an opaque keyset cursor whose predicate must stay in lockstep with an ORDER BY ending `bt.id DESC`; a malformed cursor, a non-calendar date, a non-UUID id, or a cursor combined with a non-zero `offset` all throw `InvalidCursorError` before any query.
- Parsers: ABSA is mapped by HEADER NAME (both the current and legacy layouts) and reads SA-style "1 234,56"; `YYYYMMDD` is checked before the separator split and validated with `isRealCalendarDate`. QIF strips header LINES, not whole blocks (`!Type:Bank` shares a block with transaction #1). The Reference column is matched against exact header names and left UNSET when blank. Not every format carries one: `bankCsvParserStandard` (standard_bank/capitec/nedbank), the ABSA legacy layout and every PDF parser have none.
- VLM env: `VLLM_BASE_URL`, `VLM_MODEL`, `VLLM_API_KEY`, `VLLM_TIMEOUT`; `isVlmAvailable()` for health.

## Feed lifecycle (bank sync v1)
- **Feed lifecycle (migration 675).** `bank_transactions.feed_state` is `pending | posted | removed`, independent of `status`. Manual and statement rows are `posted`. A non-posted row is visible in the review queue and nowhere else: every accounting mutation refuses it, and every statement total, coverage figure and KPI filters `feed_state = 'posted'`.
- **Three layers, all required.** (1) Locked mutators call `assertFeedPosted` from the row they hold, before the first write (`bankFeedStateGuard.ts`). (2) Set-based writers carry `feed_state = 'posted'` in their candidate predicate. (3) Trigger `trg_bank_tx_feed_state_guard` refuses any accounting-column change on a non-posted row and any source-field change on a processed feed row (SQLSTATE 23514, `BANK_TX_FEED_GUARD:`). A new writer that forgets (1) or (2) gets a 500 from (3); the trigger is a backstop, not the user-facing refusal.
- **Legal lifecycle moves:** `pending -> posted` and `pending -> removed` only.
- **Reader census ratchet.** `tests/unit/guards/bankFeedStateReaderCensus.test.ts` classifies every file whose SQL reads `bank_transactions` (filtered / exempt: reason). A new reader file must be classified; the ratchet is per file, so a new statement in an already-classified file still needs a posted predicate by hand.
- **`bank_transactions_posted` view (migration 675) is `SELECT *`**, which freezes its column list to `bank_transactions`' shape at creation time. Any later migration that drops or retypes a `bank_transactions` column must DROP and recreate `bank_transactions_posted` — a bare `ALTER TABLE` does not propagate through a `SELECT *` view.

## Recent changes
- 2026-09-13: **the provisional (AI) posting and its reversal go through the controlled bank allocation; nothing posts or reverses a generated journal directly.** `provisionalPostingService.postProvisional` built an `auto_bank_recon` journal and posted it directly — the same defect class as the rule sweep — so with `auto_post_settings.enabled` the WHOLE statement import answered 500 `CONTROL_INTEGRITY_FAILED` because of one predicted line, and `provisional/outstanding` did the same for the batch. It now calls `allocateProvisionalTransaction`, which carries a `provisional {predictedSupplierId?, confidence}` block in the plan (so the receipt's fingerprint covers the prediction) and whose effect lands the row `status='provisional'` with `provisional_je_id`, `matched_journal_line_id`, `needs_evidence=true` and `posting_agent='ai-provisional:v1'` — the bank line is deliberately recorded on a provisional row because the controlled REVERSAL proves the original allocation by it, which is why `autoPostUndoService`'s old "both set → reverse the matched line only" warning is gone and the provisional branch runs FIRST. Both import sweeps posted as a synthetic `00000000-…` user (refused as a context mismatch, poisoning on its own) and now use the request's principal, refusing outright when there is no control request. Refusals are per-row skips through `classifyAutoPostRefusal` in `autoPostGateService` too — a fault or an already-poisoned request still aborts the run. `provisional/outstanding` posts SEQUENTIALLY (one connection, one savepoint stack). The predicted cost centre and project are NOT carried onto the line (the plan validates dimensions by type; a predicted centre of the wrong type would refuse a postable line) — coding is finalised when evidence is attached. **Dismiss and undo** (`provisionalDismissService`, `autoPostUndoService`) called `reverseJournalEntry` directly and were refused for the same reason: every provisional entry in the ledger was undismissable. Both now call `reverseProvisionalEntry`, which reverses through `bank_allocation.reverse` — against the allocation's own receipt where there is one, and for the population production already holds (posted BEFORE the controls, so no intent and no receipt) against provenance PROVEN from the data: `bankAllocationLegacyProvisional` requires exactly one bank row naming the journal and still `provisional`, a posted unreversed `auto_bank_recon` journal, exactly one line on that bank account crediting the statement amount, and no payment child. Migration 840 makes `control_bank_allocation_reversal_intents.original_intent_id` nullable, adds `legacy_journal_entry_id`, and CHECKs that exactly one of the two is set. A provenance refusal is a 400 with its reason, not a 500.
- 2026-09-12 (final review): **an approval policy the kernel cannot evaluate is a data-state refusal, not a 500 on every import.** `POST /api/accounting/approval-rules` (`approvalService.createRule`) validates neither operator nor threshold, so a `payment` rule with `condition_operator='less_than'` or a negative value made `matchApprovalRules` throw a plain 'Unsupported approval policy' from the sweep's approval question — a fault — and every statement import for every rule-bearing account answered 500. The three policy throws in `controls/approvalRuleService` ('Unsupported approval policy', 'Invalid approval policy threshold', 'Approval policy population exceeds execution limit') are now `OperationRefusalError`: every line is counted `refused` with that text and the import lands; the manual allocation under such a rule stays a 400 as before. **Follow-up, not done here: validate operator/threshold in `createRule`.** Also: `bank-rules-action` no longer logs a fault it rethrows (withErrorHandler logs it and reports to Sentry); `extension-ingest`'s fault path is stated correctly — withErrorHandler answers 500 and RETURNS, and `withExtensionToken` COMMITs regardless of status, so the imported rows and the `failed` sync-log row are kept and a retry dedupes (`tests/unit/api/extensionIngestFaultCommits.test.ts` keeps the real error handler to see it).

- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r4): the undo-anyway projection is REAL balances (`autoPostUndoProjection`: net of every posted line on each touched account, minus the posting's effect after) — a posting-plus-one-journal sum hid one overstatement per dialog on a split correction. The scan bound is POSTING TIME only; the `entry_date` bound was not what bought the speed and it let a backdated (month-end) reclass through. `autoPostHandOffset` / `autoPostHandCorrection` are classified in `bankFeedStateReaderCensus` as exempt: their `bank_transactions` reads are keyed on `provisional_je_id` / `matched_journal_line_id` / `auto_post_run_id`, which a non-posted feed row cannot carry (trigger 675).
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r3): a blocking journal that does NOT net the posting out (a reclass, a partial correction) gets "reverse that journal first, then undo" — once reversed through the product the chain walk sees it off the books and the undo nets to zero; "mark as corrected" is offered only when it nets out; "undo anyway" shows each account now and after the undo (`autoPostUndoProjection`) before anyone confirms. Undo-anyway refuses (400, declaration rolled back) any outcome that is not an undo — a line reconciled meanwhile, a re-reversed posting. The scan was bounded by entry_date here; r4 dropped that (see below). Per-journal line checks compare `company_id::TEXT` so stale statistics cannot pick the company-wide index (8,000 earlier or later journals: ≤ 88 ms stale or analyzed).
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r2): detection FAILS CLOSED — any later person-made journal (source not `auto_*`, `posting_agent` human/legacy or NULL) that moves a NON-bank account of the posting back blocks the undo, so a reclass (the common hand correction) is caught; the bank leg alone never blocks. "Mark as corrected" is decided by the NET (posting + journal = 0 on every non-bank account), so a later receipt can no longer close a live posting; "Not the correction — undo anyway" is the second recorded choice. The scan is one statement per row bounded by the posting's non-bank accounts: 8,000 later bank journals cost 5–25 ms (was 2,874 ms). Known: a person-made credit to an expense account after a posting blocks every earlier auto-posting on it until the user decides.
- 2026-09-11 (R-079): `undoRun` no longer reverses a posting a person already offset with a MANUAL journal (no `reversal_of_id`, no `reversed_at` — the undo applied the correction twice, E1 ending −60 with the run read undone). Decided by ledger evidence, never by an equal amount alone: a later posted non-reversal journal still on the books that moves the posting's accounts back AND is either linked (source record = the bank line, or the posting's source document) or person-made, owned by no other bank line, and wholly within the posting (only its accounts, opposite direction, ≤ the posted amount). Such a row is skipped `offsetByHand`; the user reverses their journal or confirms it via `markCorrectedByHand`. Known limit: a reclass to an account the posting never touched is indistinguishable from an unrelated one and does not stop the undo. `docs/audits/remediation/R-079/fix.md`.
- 2026-09-10: `save_dimensions` validates CC1, CC2 and business-unit references through the journal assignment policy before updating `bank_transactions`. This closes the direct-save bypass: inactive, foreign, missing or wrong-slot assignments are refused before the write, while allocation itself continues through the same shared policy when it creates its journal.
- 2026-09-10 (K-071/K-074 review r13): the census above was re-derived THROUGH intermediaries and found four more routes — `bank-transactions-action`, `bank-transactions-manual`, `supplier-payments-action`, `customer-payments-action` — each answering contention from a blanket catch (400, and 500 on the manual one). `core/retryableContention.isRetryableContention` unions the four predicates and each route tests it before its blanket branch; `k071-void-lock-order.int.test.ts` now pins 409 instead of `< 500`, which passed at both. R-060 registers the blanket catches themselves as a partial-commit hazard for non-aborting throws.
- 2026-09-10 (K-071/K-074 review r11): the 409-for-contention rule reached the four DIRECT-importer routes, not just the two confirm arms — `ar/receipt-match/confirm.ts` and `customer-allocations.ts` now test `isRetryableReceiptRefusal` before the 400 branch, and `supplier-allocations.ts` gained the whole classifier (409 for `isPaymentLockTimeout` or `isRetryableSupplierPaymentRefusal`, 400 only for a typed `SupplierPaymentRefusal`, re-throw for everything else), which required typing `planSupplierPaymentApplication`'s four bare-`Error` refusals. The branch's own integration tests `k071-{bill,invoice}-lock-concurrency` asserted the old 400 and now assert 409.
- 2026-09-09 (K-071/K-074 + review): `bank-match-confirm`'s supplier arm moved to `confirmSupplierMatch.ts` (settles through `ap/supplierBankPaymentService`) and its CUSTOMER arm to `confirmCustomerMatch.ts` (settles through `ar/receiptMatchConfirmService`) — the customer branch wrote `amount_paid` absolutely with no allocation row, so a reversal returned the credit to AR control and left the invoice reading as paid; the import auto-post sweep runs in `withSavepoint('bank_import_autopost_<n>')`. Refusals are now TYPED rather than message-matched — `SupplierPaymentRefusal`, `BankAllocationRefusal`, `isBankTransactionLockTimeout` — so the route answers 400 / 409 for a pre-write refusal and keeps 500 for everything after the first write. `customer-allocations.ts` answers a contended payment 409 with the retry wording rather than re-throwing it into a 500 whose text `internalError` replaces, and logs a refusal below error level so a user's own mistake is not monitored as a fault.
- **STILL OPEN, named not fixed:** a transfer rule is not RECORDED as a transfer. `bank_categorisation_rules` has no transfer column, so the sweep posts `source:'auto_bank_recon'`, `allocation_type='account'`, no `counterparty_account_id`, no `transfer_journal_entry_id`, and none of `allocateTransaction`'s duplicate-transfer guard — the same movement can be posted again from the counterparty bank's feed. Amounts right, shape wrong; giving rules a transfer shape is a schema change. Also open: `invoiceSkipReason` (`allocationApplyRoute`) is exported and called by nothing — left in place, since wiring it up is a behaviour change; and `vlmBankMatchService` has no callers.
- 2026-09-09: **`bulkAcceptTransactions` over-reported success for rows it never touched.** It read `.count` off an UPDATE with no `RETURNING` — always undefined — and fell back to `ids.length`, so the operator was told every id they sent had been accepted, including rows the `status IN ('imported','allocated')` predicate skipped. `deleteTransactions` twenty lines above already carried both the `RETURNING id` and the comment explaining why; this is the instance that comment did not cover. Now `RETURNING id` + `result.length`. Worse than the K-111 defect it neighbours: that one under-reported to zero, this one reported success that had not happened.

## Forensic allocation writer checkpoint

`prepareBankAllocation(ctx, plan)` persists immutable exact-decimal account/split/customer/supplier instructions without posting. `executeBankAllocation(ctx, intentId, {approvalId?})` uses payment approval policies and the shared parent kernel; generated journals preserve kind-specific source with source_record_id equal to the bank transaction ID. The effect atomically writes the journal, selected child receipt/payment applications, bank status and protected child history. Receipt retries recheck current/original authority and actual journal/payment observations. Legacy allocate/split adapters delegate this service. Explicit invoice applications are fixed in the intent; refund/transfer, auto-selection, dimensions and reversal acceptance remain separately pending.
